```{r}

library(Benchmarking)
library(knitr)

# Facility names
facilities <- paste("Facility", 1:6)

# Inputs: staff hours and supplies
X <- cbind(
  Staff_Hours = c(150, 400, 320, 520, 350, 320),
  Supplies    = c(0.2, 0.7, 1.2, 2.0, 1.2, 0.7)
)

```
```{r}
# Outputs, in thousands
Y <- cbind(
  Third_Party_Patient_Days = c(14, 14, 42, 28, 19, 14),
  Private_Patient_Days     = c(3.5, 21, 10.5, 42, 25, 15)
)
rownames(X) <- facilities
rownames(Y) <- facilities

#Assignment model names
model_codes <- c(
  FDH = "fdh",
  VRS = "vrs",
  DRS = "drs",
  IRS = "irs",
  CRS = "crs",
  FRH = "add"
)

```

```{r}
#Objects to store results

models <- list()

# Facility by Model efficiency table.
efficiency_table <- data.frame(
  Facility = facilities
)

# Peer and lambda table
all_peer_lambdas <- data.frame(
  Model = character(),
  Facility_Evaluated = character(),
  Peer_Facility = character(),
  Lambda = numeric()
)

```

```{r}
#Running every model and printing result

for (model_name in names(model_codes)) {
  cat("\n")
  cat("====================================================\n")
  cat("MODEL:", model_name, "\n")
  cat("RTS CODE:", model_codes[[model_name]], "\n")
  cat("====================================================\n")

  model_fit <- dea(
    X,
    Y,
    RTS = model_codes[[model_name]]
  )

  # Save all results
  models[[model_name]] <- model_fit

#Print efficiency scores and add scores to final efficiency table
  model_efficiency <- data.frame(
    Facility = facilities,
    Efficiency = round(model_fit$eff, 4)
  )

  cat("\nEfficiency Scores:\n")
  print(model_efficiency)

  # Add this model's scores to the final efficiency table.
  efficiency_table[[model_name]] <- round(model_fit$eff, 4)

#Print peers and lambdas
 
lambda_matrix <- model_fit$lambda

  # Force readable row and column names.
  rownames(lambda_matrix) <- facilities
  colnames(lambda_matrix) <- facilities

  # Convert lambda matrix into a long table.
  peer_lambda_table <- as.data.frame(as.table(lambda_matrix))

  names(peer_lambda_table) <- c(
    "Facility_Evaluated",
    "Peer_Facility",
    "Lambda"
  )

  # Keep only actual peers: lambda values greater than zero.
  peer_lambda_table <- subset(
    peer_lambda_table,
    Lambda > 0.000001
  )

  # Add model name and clean the output.
  peer_lambda_table$Model <- model_name
  peer_lambda_table$Lambda <- round(peer_lambda_table$Lambda, 4)

  peer_lambda_table <- peer_lambda_table[
    , c("Model", "Facility_Evaluated", "Peer_Facility", "Lambda")
  ]

  cat("\nPeers and Nonzero Lambdas:\n")
  print(peer_lambda_table)

  # Add this model's peer/lambda results to the combined table.
  all_peer_lambdas <- rbind(
    all_peer_lambdas,
    peer_lambda_table
  )
}

```


```{r}
#Print final facility and model score table; 
#Also print the final peer/lambda table

cat("\n")
cat("====================================================\n")
cat("FINAL EFFICIENCY TABLE\n")
cat("====================================================\n")

knitr::kable(
  efficiency_table,
  caption = "Final Efficiency Scores",
  digits = 4,
  align = "lrrrrrr"
)


cat("\n")
cat("====================================================\n")
cat("FINAL PEER AND LAMBDA TABLE\n")
cat("====================================================\n")
knitr::kable(
  all_peer_lambdas,
  caption = "Final Peer and Lambda Table",
  digits = 4,
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "r")
)
```
The DEA results indicate that Facilities 1–4 are efficient under all six assumptions. Facility 5 is inefficient under DRS and CRS, with an efficiency score of 0.9775, which means they could reduce input by 2.3% and produce the same output if operating under assumptions of decreasing returns to scale or constant returns to scale . Facility 6 is the least efficient, scoring 0.8963 under VRS and IRS and 0.8675 under DRS and CRS. That means facility 6 could reduce inputs by 10.4% or 13.3% depending on which assumptions are made about returns to scale. FDH and FRH classify all facilities as efficient. Overall, CRS and DRS identify greater inefficiency than VRS and IRS, while FDH and FRH provide no differentiation among facilities in this dataset.
